purpose: the source ledger that makes 'no outside material entered anonymously' checkable. Nothing here authorizes ingestion; it defines the record and the rubric.

required_fields.source_item_id: string, the identifier of the specific item within that dataset
required_fields.source_version: string, release tag, commit hash, or archive checksum of the exact bytes read
required_fields.license: string, the declared license of THOSE BYTES
required_fields.attribution_required: bool | string, the required attribution string if any
required_fields.content_hash: sha256 of the exact item bytes read

record_schema.note: license is a property of the BYTES, not of the dataset's reputation. A permissive dataset homepage does not license a specific mirror.

four_permission_flags.training_allowed: may the item's content be used as model training input
four_permission_flags.synthetic_seeding_allowed: may the item seed generation of synthetic data. This is the flag that open benchmarks most often restrict, and it is the one that matters most for v3, because v3's whole method is expansion around a root.
four_permission_flags.redistribution_allowed: may the item's content itself be redistributed inside the bank

the_global_piqa_precedent.why_recorded: the reason a boolean ledger is not optional
the_global_piqa_precedent.case: Global PIQA is CC BY-SA 4.0 but its card states it may not be used to train AI systems OR to generate synthetic training data seeded from it
the_global_piqa_precedent.lesson: 'open benchmark' does not mean 'legal seed material', and a permissive license can still forbid exactly the operation v3 performs most
the_global_piqa_precedent.consequence: synthetic_seeding_allowed is a first-class field, defaults to FALSE on any ambiguity, and no root may be ingested with it false

defaults.on_ambiguity: all four permission flags default to FALSE and the source is held at HELD_PENDING_REVIEW
defaults.code_license_does_not_transfer_to_data: a generator repo's license does not license a separately hosted dataset derived from it; this is the documented ProofWriter / RuleTaker wrinkle

admissibility_rubric.note: a source is admissible as a SEMANTIC ROOT only if it clears every criterion. A source can still be used as a challenge panel or as renderer inspiration while failing this rubric.

criteria.criterion: all four permission flags resolved to true, with the license recorded for the exact bytes read

criteria.why: v3 expands families around each root; a source that forbids synthetic seeding cannot be a root

criteria.criterion: the source provides structure attached, not just text: evidence spans, supporting-fact sets, influence graphs, proof trees, or equivalent handles
criteria.why: generic human-written QA without attached structure gives text, not capability supervision

criteria.criterion: the item is reconstructible into the v2 fact language (AT, CONNECTED, BLOCKED, HOLDS, CONTAINS, STATE, REL)
criteria.note: non-blocking as a criterion because it is a MEASUREMENT, not a property; it decides selection after probing, not before

criteria.criterion: the source's original TEST partitions are excluded from root harvesting
criteria.why: benchmark test partitions stay untouched as external transfer checks

candidate_inventory.disclaimer: Permissions were resolved against primary sources on 2026-09-30 and recorded in o1-permission-verification.json. NO source cleared rubric A2 (synthetic_seeding_allowed), so none is admitted as a semantic root. See the receipt for per-source verdicts, blocking flags, and cross-cutting findings F1-F5.
